verdicts.evidence: FALSE GREEN, verified by exit code, and three further observations in three other shapes. (1) m2, whose only defect is the cell `file:code/b.ts#a.b`: `check --strict --json` went from **exit 1 to exit 0** and the violation `Topology · topology-sovereignty-by-data-class · typed pointer file:code/b.ts#a.b — symbol "a.b" not found in the file (moved or renamed? update the pointer)` disappeared. The gate stopped refusing a pointer that names something the file does not contain. (2) m5, whose only cell is the honest `file:code/b.ts#"the sealed promise"` over a file carrying `the sealed promiseX`: **exit 0 to exit 1**, with the new violation `typed pointer file:code/b.ts#"the sealed promise" — symbol "the sealed promise" not found in the file` — an honest pointer turned RED. (3) m1 moved in both directions inside one run: the `#a.b` violation REMOVED and the `#"the sealed promise"` violation ADDED, exit staying 1 (so an exit-code-only instrument would have reported nothing). (4) m4, whose only cell is `file:code/b.ts#[companion`: the mutant produced **zero bytes on stdout** and died with `✗ Invalid regular expression: /(?<![\w$])[companion(?![\w$])/: Unmatched ')'` — `check --strict --json` rendered no JSON at all, so an agent driving on the ADR-0030 machine contract gets no verdict. Ledgers: reports/mutation/probe-symbolPresent-{m1,m2,m4,m5,m3,m6,selfgate}.jsonl. Mechanism, read off the four observations rather than off the code: dropping the `^` makes the identifier test accept any symbol that merely ENDS in an identifier run, so dotted names, quoted sentences and bracketed text are interpolated into a `RegExp` — where `.` becomes a wildcard, a trailing word character defeats the `(?![\w$])` boundary, and an unbalanced `[` is a syntax error. Note the blast radius is wider than `check`: `dist/lib/spec-conformance.js` imports `symbolPresent` for `spec-check` (see src/lib/spec-conformance.ts:77), so the same flip lands there too.

Verified by exit code. On m3, whose only cell is `file:code/deleted-j.ts<U+2028> a trailing note` and whose cited file does not exist, `check --strict --json` went from **exit 0 to exit 1**, gaining `Topology · topology-sovereignty-by-data-class · typed pointer does not resolve: file:code/deleted-j.ts — update it or remove the row`. On m1 the same mutant added `Handover · handover-agents-charter-final · typed pointer does not resolve: file:code/deleted-k.ts` (same cell shape), exit staying 1. Identical payloads on m2, m4, m5, m6 and the self-gate, none of which carries an interior line terminator. Ledgers: reports/mutation/probe-symbolPresent-{m1,m3,m2,m4,m5,m6,selfgate}.jsonl; details captured with scripts/probe-detail.mjs. What the measurement shows is uncomfortable and is the reason this is filed rather than cleared: the mutant is STRICTER than the shipped code. The `$` anchor is exactly what makes an invisible U+2028 (or CR) left in a cell swallow a typed pointer — `.` cannot cross a line terminator, so `(\S.*)$` never reaches the end and the whole pointer vanishes while the row still reads as evidence and the deleted file is never opened. That is the RWD-2026-0006 family (docs/compliance/known-defects.md:41, 'silent no-op pointers that looked precise and verified nothing'), alive in the shipped 0.36.0 build and measured here on m3's baseline: exit 0 over a cell citing a file that does not exist. Nothing in the suite pins the anchor in either direction, so a change to this constant — in either direction — is unobserved.
